sources.entry: Audio Priority Bar - Native macOS menu bar app that automatically switches to your highest-priority connected headphones, speakers, and microphone.

summary.one_liner: A native macOS menu bar app that ranks your headphones, speakers, and microphones and automatically switches to the highest-ranked one that is connected.
summary.what_it_does: Lets you drag audio outputs and microphones into a priority order from a menu bar panel, and switches the Mac to the top connected device when devices connect or disconnect. It can switch back when macOS or another app changes the device on its own, such as AirPods being put in. It offers a global mute shortcut (⌥ ⇧ M) and URL-based controls for mute and automatic switching. Profiles store separate device orders for setups like Desk, Meeting, or Travel. It also lets you connect and disconnect paired Bluetooth devices from the panel and shows battery levels for AirPods and Jabra headsets on a Link dongle.
use_cases: Automatically switch audio to headphones when they connect
Keep sound on a preferred speaker when a display connects
Mute the microphone across all apps with a keyboard shortcut
Control audio devices from Shortcuts, Raycast, or a Stream Deck
Switch between audio setups using profiles or Focus modes
Connect or disconnect paired Bluetooth headphones from the menu bar
how_to_run: Or download AudioPriorityBar.zip from the releases page, unzip it, and move AudioPriorityBar.app to /Applications
If macOS blocks the first launch, open System Settings > Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway
Requires macOS 14 Sonoma or later, on Apple silicon or Intel
notable: Ranked device priority with automatic switching and a brief notice naming the device it picked
Global mute hotkey (⌥ ⇧ M) and URL scheme commands usable from Shortcuts, Raycast, or Stream Deck
Profiles with a Focus filter to apply device orders automatically
Direct Jabra Link dongle query to detect when a wireless headset is powered off
Shortcuts app actions for setting output, microphone, mute, and automatic switching
caveats: Signed with its own certificate, not an Apple Developer ID, and not notarized, so first launch may need manual approval
Jabra Link 390 support is unverified on hardware; only Link 380 is hardware-verified
Some features need permissions such as Bluetooth, Input Monitoring, and Accessibility, and Open at Login may need approval
